title: DuckNet backlog groom — findings
description: Output of the groom stage. One flat findings array with a kind discriminator rather than one array per concern, so the same merge-confidence.sh join works here as in backlog-build. No confidence field: an independent pass scores it.

summary.description: One to three sentences on the shape and health of the backlog as a whole.

backlog_size.description: How many issues were read. Zero means the dump was empty or unreadable.

id.description: Stable kebab-case slug, e.g. group-consumer-base-extraction or refine-25-acceptance. Stable across runs so a recurring finding is recognisable.

kind.description: refinement: the issue is not ready to pick up. grouping: several issues are one user story or epic. duplicate: two issues are the same work. stale: the premise no longer holds in the code. gap: work the code or documents imply that no issue covers. ordering: one issue must land before another.

issues.description: Issue numbers this finding concerns. Empty only for kind gap.

severity.description: blocker: nobody can pick this up as written. major: it will cost a round-trip. minor: tidying.

detail.description: What is wrong or what the relationship is, and what to do about it.

missing.description: kind refinement: what the issue lacks.

suggested_title.description: kind refinement or grouping: a better title.

suggested_body.description: kind refinement: a rewritten body a human can paste. kind grouping: the parent user story or epic body, including a task list of its children.

keep.description: kind duplicate: which issue number to keep.

blocked_by.description: kind ordering: issue numbers that must land first.

evidence.description: kind stale or gap: what in the code supports the claim.

notes.description: Observations that did not clear the bar, and anything about the backlog as a whole. Empty array if none.
